title: Monotonicity of non-three-colorability
statement: For any fixed number $v$ of vertices, regard a graph on the vertex set $\{0,\ldots,v-1\}$ as a choice of edges, each an unordered pair of distinct vertices. If such a graph $G$ has no proper coloring with three colors, then every graph on the same vertex set containing all the edges of $G$ also has no proper coloring with three colors.
hypotheses_covered: The second graph contains every edge of the first graph
The first graph is not three-colorable
